newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin Wall guards convicted for '62 Wall shooting.
newsitem.headline: Berlin Wall guards convicted for '62 Wall shooting.

text.p: A Berlin court convicted two former East German border guards of manslaughter on Wednesday for the 1962 killing of Peter Fechter, a mason who was shot and bled to death at the Berlin Wall as his cries for help went unheeded.

Judge Hans-Juergen Schaal said the two-day trial had not been able to fully determine which guard had fired the fatal shot that caused one of the most grisly deaths at the Berlin Wall, but he said both guards were still guilty of manslaughter. They were given suspended sentences following a pattern established in previous Wall shooting trials.

"It is legally irrelevant that it could not be proven that either of the guards fired the deadly shot," Schaal said. "Joint manslaughter was committed here because neither of you consciously tried to miss the target."

Schaal handed a 21-month sentence of probation to Rolf Friedrich, now 61, and a 20-month sentence of probation to Erich Schreiber for shooting 17-year-old Fechter, hit in the pelvis while running toward the Berlin Wall near an Allied checkpoint.

Fechter had called in vain for help for about 50 minutes as he slowly bled to death. Of the 235 people killed at the Berlin Wall that divided the city during the Cold War, Fechter's agonised death was the most famous.
"I am sorry and would like to apologise to his sister," said Friedrich after the verdict was read. Fechter's sister Ruth had followed the trial from the courtroom gallery.
Schaal said that it was completely unacceptable that no one came to Fechter's aid as he lay bleeding next to the Wall. But he said the two guards could not be held responsible for that.
The East German guards did not provide first aid because there was no senior officer on duty in that section of the Wall who had the authority to order assistance.
Fechter's anguished screams were ignored by East German border guards, although West Berlin police and Western Allies tried vainly to help by tossing first aid kits over the Wall.
Because Fechter was on Soviet-controlled East Berlin territory, West Berlin police said they could not intervene.
Hundreds of people who heard Fechter's cries gathered on the western side of the Wall shouting "murderers, murderers" at the East German border guards.

The horrifying accounts of Fechter's death and dramatic pictures of East German police carrying his limp body away from the Wall were published around the world and prompted widespread condemnation of the Wall and the East German regime.
Berlin's mayor places a wreath of flowers each year on August 17 -- the date of Fechter's killing -- at a cross next to the spot at the Wall where he was shot.
Fechter and his friend Helmut Kulbeik had been planning to flee for about five months. Both were working at a construction site in East Berlin on August 17, 1962.

During their lunch break they hid in a building near the Wall, burying themselves in a pile of sawdust before their dash to the Wall at a point just a few hundred metres (yards) from Checkpoint Charlie crossing point.

Fechter climbed through a window in the East Berlin building, jumped over a line of barbed wire and ran towards the Wall. He was just 10 metres (yards) from it when a bullet from a machine gun hit him.
